      <title>California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/20/california-coastal-communities-alert-big-waves-hit-state</link>
      <description><p>Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded</p><p>Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.</p><p>Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/20/california-coastal-communities-alert-big-waves-hit-state">Continue reading...</a></description>

Jamaica usually conjures up images of white sandy beaches, Rastafari culture and Bob Marley – but another reality exists. On this small Caribbean island, less than 1 percent of the coastline is freely accessible to local people. The rest has gradually been privatised, mostly for large hotel developments and private homes.  
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1952df8c-e41e-11f1-b8ec-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/Reporters-3.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1952df8c-e41e-11f1-b8ec-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/Reporters-3.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">e9372ab0-e431-11f1-9387-ff4fa45f9015</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:55:10 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Laurence CUVILLIER</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Cincinnati Zoo's famed Fiona the hippo dies days after eating a visitor’s hat</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261120-cincinnati-zoo-s-famed-fiona-the-hippo-dies-days-after-eating-a-visitor-s-hat</link><description>
Fiona, the hippo whose premature birth and fight for survival at the Cincinnati Zoo turned her into a global sensation nearly a decade ago, died Thursday from complications after swallowing a knit hat that was accidentally flung into her enclosure. She was 9 years old. “It is with extreme sadness that we share with you the devastating news that Fiona did not make it after multiple attempts from our amazing vets and keeper team to help her through what ended up being a medical emergency,” the zoo said in a statement.

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/28039ada-e4f0-11f1-9a52-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261120-140752-144607-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/28039ada-e4f0-11f1-9a52-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261120-140752-144607-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2d05e272-e4f0-11f1-9bcb-bf5d2765226b</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:45:20 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>COP31 wrapping up in Turkey: Climate deal elusive as fossil fuels go unmentioned</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261120-cop31-wrapping-up-in-turkey-climate-deal-elusive-as-fossil-fuels-go-unmentioned</link><description>
The UN's COP31 climate talks were set to spill into overtime Friday as countries remained deadlocked over a draft deal that makes no mention of fossil fuels, with a host of other disputes also snarling negotiations. FRANCE 24's Environment Editor Valerie Dekimpe tells us more.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/846de880-e4ef-11f1-8515-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261120-151225-151557-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/846de880-e4ef-11f1-8515-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261120-151225-151557-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">89987e06-e4ef-11f1-89be-770637ba5815</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:38:56 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Burnham hails 'landmark' EU-UK deal as 'good day' for Britain, Europe</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261120-burnham-hails-landmark-eu-uk-deal-as-good-day-for-britain-europe</link><description>

The Himalayas tower below the clouds, capped in icy snow in new snapshots captured from aboard the International Space Station.

What is it?

Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk was looking out one of the windows aboard the space station when the most incredible view came into focus  — and thankfully he had a camera handy and was able to capture these striking scenes of the Himalayas from space.

Above the mountain range, fluffy clouds hang in the atmosphere. Below, the expansive Himalayas are covered in bright snow and ice, which looks somehow both white and blue at the same time as the bright sunlight streaks across the breathtaking expanse.

This frosty winter scene showcases the mountain range from orbit, from about 250 miles (400 kilometers) above Earth's surface. But even from this distance, the magnitude of this mountain range is palpable. The Himalayas stretch across five different countries including Nepal, India, China, Bhutan and Pakistan. And the Himalayas include some of the highest mountain peaks on planet Earth, including Mount Everest.

Why is it incredible?

From orbit around Earth, you might expect even the largest landmarks on our planet to appear miniscule. But somehow, in these photographs snapped by Kutryk during NASA's SpaceX Crew-13 mission, even from hundreds of miles above our planet you can really see and feel the immense scale of this mammoth mountain range.

It's unclear exactly where above the mountain range these photographs were taken, but it is always amazing to think that within these sweeping landscapes are people living their lives, likely unaware that an astronaut is taking in the beauty of their home.

Perhaps somewhere hidden under the clouds in one of Kutryk's photographs are hikers climbing up the side of Mt. Everest, completing their own bucket list adventure as the astronauts watching from above complete theirs.

]]> <![CDATA[ I got to tour SpaceX's Starfactory facility in Starbase, Texas, and what I saw blew my mind ]]> STARBASE, Texas  — I just finished covering the Starship Flight 15 mission, and SpaceXs incredible launch tower catch of the returned Ship 42 spacecraft isn't the only thing over the weekend that left me speechless.

The morning of the launch (Nov. 13), SpaceX invited media on a tour of Starbase's Starfactory facility, where it manufactures and assembles both stages of its massive Starship rocket - an unprecedented behind-the-scenes look at the production and scale of SpaceX's operations, and a glimpse of things to come as Starship notches more and more milestones the more it flies.

For some context, the five-story-tall Starfactory spans approximately 1 million square feet (~93,000 meters), with operations split between Starship's Super Heavy boosters and upper stage Ships, and nearly 330,000 additional square feet (30,000 square meters) of office space. SpaceX officials describe its design as one more akin to an automotive manufacturing plant than that of a typical aerospace production site, and inside, it is absolutely alive with activity.

Inside Starfactory

We entered through an arch-covered doorway underneath the giant "X" sign on the building's shorter face. Our media gaggle was met with curious glances as we were shown through the doors and guided onto the factory floor - few are ever able to cross that threshold outside of SpaceX employees, and our presence seemed as novel to those busy working as it was to us.

Inside, we were struck with the sheer enormity of Starship's scale. Giant stainless-steel rocket parts were meticulously scattered across different subassembly stations throughout the building, with Ship nose cones, cylindrical sections and booster components all under various stages of manufacture. The sheer quantity of the hardware was staggering, and being so close to each as we walked Starfactory's throughways was an eye-opener.

Starbase is a unique partnership of privately-owned SpaceX property and publicly-accessible land and shoreline, which has created the unique ability for anyone with a mind to do so to drive right up to the the Starship launch pad to see the facilities up close (within a few hundred feet or so, which, as rockets go, is very, very close).

Fully stacked, Starship stands more than 400 feet (120 meters) tall. Standing next to such a towering colossus on the pad is enough to drive home just how big the launch vehicle is, but standing next its segmented components inside Starfactory is even more humbling; like seeing one of Ship's upper aerodynamic flaps, which are each large enough when laid flat that you could park a pair of large SUVs on their faces with room to spare.

As our tour continued and we passed rows of nose cones under preparation for integration, numbering as high as Ship 51, one stood out from the others. In the distance, only visible for moment between the overlapping views of other Ships as we walked through the production stations, was a nose cone with a series of windows cut out of its face - undoubtedly a prototype for, or possibly even the final article that will be used as NASA's Artemis lunar lander.

NASA has contracted SpaceX to develop a version of Starship capable of landing astronauts on the moon as a part of the agency's Artemis program, and this appeared to the Ship being readied for when that mission arrives. NASA is targeting Artemis IV as the program's first crewed lunar landing in 2028, and while the decision solidifying Starship as the lander tasked with that mission isn't finalized (Blue Origin is also vying for that spot with its Blue Moon lander), SpaceX is clearly operating with the intention of coming out ahead.

But Artemis is clearly not SpaceX's only focus, as evident by the many, many other Ships in production that did not have window holes carved out of them.SpaceX officials said the company is currently completing about one Ship upper stage every two weeks, and one Super Heavy booster every four weeks, with overlapping production allowing multiple rockets to move through the factory simultaneously. The majority of the vehicles currently being assembled will carry stacks of SpaceX's upgraded Starlink Version 3 (V3) satellites.

The company's Starlink network in low Earth orbit currently consists of more than 11,000 spacecraft beaming wireless internet to SpaceX customers across the globe. All of those were launched on SpaceX's workhorse Falcon 9 rocket, with the exception of a few more than 50 delivered on Starship's two most recent test flights. Both carried V3 Starlink stacks to add to the constellation, which SpaceX officials say each added the data capacity equivalent to ten Falcon 9 Starlink launches. And, as they fine tune Starship's design, SpaceX plans to increase the vehicle's launch cadence dramatically, growing the Starlink network as it does.

SpaceX CEO Elon Musk has stated the company hopes to launch Starship about once a week beginning in 2027, and with the number of Ships we saw lined up inside Starfactory, launch vehicle inventory doesn't seem like it will be to blame if that goal isn't realized.

Building rockets like cars (and Lego bricks)

SpaceX has adopted a manufacturing process modeled after the automotive industry, where efficiency and reproduction allow for the manufacture of large numbers of identical parts. Automation is a critical part of that process, but not one SpaceX is ready to entirely rely on.

Much of the equipment and tools being used for Starship's production were designed by SpaceX engineers, who are constantly refining production processes to eliminate bottlenecks. And SpaceX has deliberately kept technicians on the floor as Starship's design continues to evolve, rather than automating procedures that might soon become obsolete.

Our tour guide compared SpaceX's manufacturing consistency goals to that of Lego bricks, which are famously precise in their production down to the micro-millimeter accuracy of what now number more than 1 trillion bricks made since the toy company began in the 1940s.

Expansion

Exiting the far side of the building, we stood in the shadow of SpaceX's two towering Mega Bays, where the sections of Starship are stacked and integrated with their engines - there's one hanger for Ship, and another for Super Heavy. Each can hold about five or six assemblies, and housed two or three vehicles at the time our tour was brought by.

Both Mega Bays, however, looked small against the adjacent Gigabay SpaceX is currently constructing. At approximately 700,000 square feet (65,000 square meters), Gigabay will be equipped with room to accommodate up to 24 vehicles at a time, and will facilitate a major increase in SpaceX's ability to assemble its Ship and Super Heavy rockets.

Part of SpaceX's goal with Starship is to make all of what we got to see completely routine; to make rocket launches and landings as ordinary as commercial airline flights. Still, standing inside Starfactory, surrounded on all sides by huge spacecraft in various stages of assembly, it was hard to imagine a reality where giant rockets flying to and from space on a regular basis wouldn't feel like science fiction.

Later that day a giant rocket launched to outer space - Super Heavy did attempt a return to pad, but was diverted for an offshore landing instead, where it exploded. But the next day, Ship 42 came plunging through the overcast cloud cover, falling belly-first toward the same tower it left just a couple dozen hours before. And then it lit its engines and was caught by the tower.

That felt like science fiction too.

That, in turn, verifies Einstein's greatest theory, general relativity, which first predicted the existence of black holes and what their immediate surroundings would look like.

Team leader and researcher with Australia's Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation (CSIRO), Samuel Lai explained why capturing the image of a distant black hole is so tricky.

"It is like standing in your backyard and trying to take a photo of a doughnut on the moon," Lai said in a statement sent to Space.com via email.

Lai and his small Australian team developed advanced machine learning and artificial intelligence techniques to capture information about the black hole's structure and filter out interference resulting from the fact that the EHT was viewing M87* from within our planet's atmosphere. The machine-learning technique called GenDIReCT also accounted for biases introduced by combining telescopes to create an Earth-sized interferometer.

"When we applied it to the original EHT dataset, we found a black hole almost identical in size and shape as the historic EHT image. Importantly, our model had no idea what a black hole looked like when we applied it to the M87 data," Lai continued. "This is the first truly independent validation of the EHT image, an important step in the scientific process."

This could settle the questions of just how the final image of M87* was influenced by both atmospheric effects and the processing methods needed to reconstruct pictures from telescope data.

That's not just good news for the EHT; it's good news for Einstein.

Einstein published his theory of general relativity in 1915, completely reshaping how we think of gravity. General relativity suggested that objects with mass curve the very fabric of space and time, united as a single entity called spacetime. Gravity arises from that curvature.

The greater the mass, the more extreme the curvature and thus the greater the gravitational influence of that object. Taking this to its extreme, scientist Karl Schwarzschild came up with a solution to the equations of general relativity that suggested an infinitesimal region with infinite mass, resulting in unrestrained curvature, a singularity. Around this would be a spherical boundary at which not even light has the velocity needed to escape this region. Referred to as the Schwarzschild radius, that boundary became known as the event horizon of a black hole. The singularity, its heart.

Black holes were born in 1915, decades before their discovery and over a century before the EHT saw one.

General relativity also predicted what the region around the event horizon would look like. A ring of superheated glowing plasma with the shadow of the black hole falling on it.

When scientists first saw the image of M87* they were astounded at how close it reflected predictions made by general relativity, thus confirming the the theory once again. This verification further solidifies that development.

Verifying the EHT's image of M87* could lead to the CSIRO-developed technique being applied to some more "down-to-Earth" uses such as improving medical imaging and mapping earthquakes.

"Independent validation is at the heart of the scientific process, and it is especially valuable for results as novel as those of the EHT. It is extremely gratifying to see that GenDIReCT, an elegant, entirely independent method, recovers the ring structure of M87* across several years, in excellent agreement with the EHT Collaboration’s published results," Laurent Loinard, Director of the EHT Collaboration, said.

The team's research was published on Wednesday (Nov. 11) in the journal Nature.

]]> <![CDATA[ On this day in space! Nov. 19, 2005: Japan's Hayabusa spacecraft makes 1st-ever liftoff from surface of an asteroid ]]>

On Nov. 19, 2005, the Japanese Hayabusa spacecraft made the first liftoff from an asteroid. Hayabusa was supposed to return asteroid samples to Earth.

Asteroids are space rocks that were formed during the early solar system. We study asteroids to learn more about the solar system's history. Hayabusa (pronounced HI-uh-BOOS-uh) made two touchdowns on asteroid Itokawa (EE -toh-KA-wah). Each time, the spacecraft went into safe mode. Controllers weren't sure if Hayabusa gathered any material. But they sent the spacecraft back to Earth anyway.

Hayabusa's sample return capsule returned to Earth in June 2010. Scientists found dust of Itokawa inside the capsule, proving that it did indeed capture samples of Itokawa.

Why it mattered

The primary goal of Japan's Hayabusa mission to asteroid Itokawa was never to be the first spacecraft to liftoff from a space rock. The mission was always aimed at collecting samples from an asteroid and returning them to Earth.

It was a hard road to Itokawa for Hayabusa. The Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) launched the probe on May 9, 2003, with plans for an arrival at the asteroid in the early summer of 2005.

That asteroid arrival was delayed until September 2005 after a solar storm degraded Hayabusa's solar arrays, limiting the available power for its ion engines.

Still, Hayabusa managed to limp along its path to reach the asteroid Itokawa on Sept. 12, 2005.

Hayabusa dropped a small lander onto Itokawa, but that probe was apparently lost. Hayabusa then dropped a landing target on the asteroid, and ultimately managed to touchdown about 99 feet from the marker, JAXA has said.

During its first landing on Nov. 19, Hayabusa descended to a point just 56 feet above Itokawa before going silent for 3 hours, according to an Associated Press report. Once contact was restored, JAXA officials confirmed the probe had landed, and it eventually lifted off for a second attempt. That was the first-ever liftoff from an asteroid by a spacecraft.

"The spacecraft actually bounced off the surface a few times and spent about 39 minutes resting on the asteroid, but apparently the samplers never fired," Andrew Cheng, a Hayabusa science team member at Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory, told Space.com at the time. There was hope that some material managed to make it inside the collector anyway.

"After all the thrashing about ... there is no way to confirm that," Cheng had said. The second landing on Itokawa occured a few days later on Nov. 26, 2005.

In November 2010, five months after Hayabusa's sample-return capsule touched down in Australia, JAXA announced some good news: Hayabusa did collect 1,500 dust grains from asteroid Itokawa, samples that were jammed into the collector by the two landings, despite is collector mechanism not firing.

The ultimate success of Hayabusa spurred the creation of another sample-return mission by Japan: Hayabusa2.

That probe launched in December 2014 and arrived at asteroid Ryugu (REE-ooh-goo) in 2018. It collected its own samples and returned them to Earth in December 2020.

The Hayabusa2 probe is now on an extended mission to the asteroid 2015 BM510, which it will fly by in April 2028. It had planned to land on a strange asteroid 1998 KY26, but suffered engine trouble that made that rendezvous impossible

]]> <![CDATA[ The view from the tower: Watch Starship come in for chopsticks catch in epic slo-mo video ]]>

A new set of slo-mo videos gives us a new perspective on SpaceX's first-ever recovery of a Starship upper stage.

The company notched the milestone on Saturday (Nov. 14), when the launch tower at its Starbase site in South Texas caught Starship's Ship spacecraft with its "chopstick" arms.

You've probably seen photos and videos showing the epic snag from afar. But on Tuesday (Nov. 17), SpaceX released up-close views — a series of four slo-mo videos captured by cameras near the top of the 480-foot-tall (146 meters) tower.

"The Starbase tower chopsticks catching their first Starship. This unique architecture was designed for full and rapid reusability, enabling repeat launches and landings from the same pad," SpaceX wrote in a Tuesday X post that shared the videos, a compilation of which you can see embedded above.

Starship is the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built. Its current "V3" version stands about 408 feet (124 m) tall, and future iterations will be even larger.

As SpaceX noted in Tuesday's post, the megarocket is also designed to be fully and rapidly reusable — a first for an orbital launch system. The company plans to catch both Starship stages — Ship and the Super Heavy booster — at the launch tower, a recovery strategy designed to enable efficient inspection, refurbishment and reflight.

SpaceX planned to carry out such a double catch on this most recent test flight, Starship's 15th to date, which launched on Friday evening (Nov. 13). But Super Heavy experienced a low-fuel warning during its return to Starbase about 6.5 minutes after launch and autonomously diverted to splash down in the Gulf of Mexico.

That wasn't a huge deal for SpaceX, as it had already caught Super Heavy on three previous test flights. Snagging Ship is tougher; the upper stage returns to Earth from orbit, so it comes in faster and hotter than the booster does.

SpaceX had not even attempted a Ship catch before Flight 15. But the company managed to pull off the maneuver on its first try.

And Ship did some work in orbit before coming home: It deployed 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 broadband satellites on Flight 15, the second batch that the company has sent to low Earth orbit. The first set was deployed on Flight 14, which launched on Sept. 28.

The veteran Hayabusa2 spacecraft launched back in 2014 to collect material from the asteroid Ryugu. The spacecraft will instead target 2015 BM510, another tiny asteroid. And there will be no landing: Hayabusa2 is scheduled to make a high-speed flyby of the near-Earth object in April 2028.

The decision was announced at a Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) press conference on Tuesday (Nov. 17), a day after a Cabinet Office space policy subcommittee meeting. The final functioning thruster out of Hayabusa2's four ion engines suffered a malfunction in mid-August, according to JAXA officials, while a sensor detected unexpected erosion of the spacecraft's surface during its long voyage in space.

"The deterioration of the onboard equipment ... is becoming increasingly evident," Japan Times quoted Yuya Mimasu, team leader of the extended mission, as saying.

Despite losing the opportunity to land on KY26, the Hayabusa2 mission has been a huge success for JAXA, and the new direction promises its own intrigues. Asteroid 2015 BM510 has already attracted interest; it's the primary target of a proposal for the European Space Agency's mini-Fast mission series. Scientists describe the body as a D-type asteroid, meaning it's thought to be organic-rich and comet-like, and may have originated in the outer solar system.

Around the same time as Hayabusa2 conducts its high-speed flyby in April 2028, JAXA is also scheduled to launch its next asteroid mission, Destiny+. Launching along with ESA's Ramses mission to study Apophis, Destiny+ will first make a flyby of the infamous asteroid ahead of its very close approach to Earth in 2029 before heading to asteroid 3200 Phaethon, the parent body of the Geminid meteor shower.

]]> <![CDATA[ China rolls out rocket for launch of 1st international astronaut to Tiangong space station (video) ]]>

China's space station is set to receive its first foreign astronaut.

A Long March 2F rocket, topped with the Shenzhou-24 crew spacecraft, was rolled out to the pad at Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China, on Tuesday (Nov. 17), with launch expected in the next week.

The 191-foot-tall (58 meters) rocket was transferred 0.93 miles (1.5 kilometers) from a vertical integration building to the pad over the course of around two hours, starting around 4 a.m. EST (0900 GMT, or 5 p.m. Beijing Time), according to China Central Television (CCTV).

China's human spaceflight agency, CMSA, stated that all facilities and equipment at the launch site are in good condition, adding that the launch is scheduled to take place in the coming days, without providing a date.

CMSA typically holds a press conference at Jiuquan a day ahead of launch, during which the crew for the mission is revealed to the public. This time, one of the three crew members will, for the first time, be an international astronaut. One of two Pakistani astronaut candidates will fly to the Tiangong space station on Shenzhou-24, marking a first both for China's outpost and for Pakistan, which will see one its astronauts reach orbit for the first time.

Though public details are sparse, it is thought that the Pakistani astronaut, operating as a payload specialist, will stay aboard Tiangong for around a week, returning home on the departing Shenzhou-23 spacecraft.

One of the three Shenzhou-23 astronauts — who are approaching the end of their six-month-long mission, having launched on May 24 — will stay aboard Tiangong for another half a year. This will provide the international visitor with a seat home on Shenzhou-23, and allow a Chinese astronaut to make the country's first year-long stay in orbit. This extra-long mission will supply China with data on physiology ahead of crewed lunar flights and other long-duration missions.

China approved its human spaceflight program in 1992 and launched its first orbital crewed mission in 2003, with Yang Liwei becoming the first Chinese national in space. The country then completed the three-module Tiangong space station in late 2022 and has kept the orbital outpost constantly crewed ever since, with rotating six-month-long missions with brief handovers between crews.

Shenzhou-24 will be China's 18th crewed mission and will mark the first time a foreign national is flying on a Shenzhou spacecraft. China is also looking to double the size of Tiangong in the coming years, potentially opening the way to further international missions and space tourist visits.

   <description>České domácnosti čeká změna v půjčování peněz. Začátkem příštího roku začne platit novela zákona výrazně zpřísňující pravidla pro poskytování spotřebitelských úvěrů.    <description>Škrtila koťata a vší silou s nimi házela o silnici, uškrtila i dva psy, ač ji měli rádi. Zapálila kůlnu a dva stohy. Nenáviděla lidi a strašně moc chtěla zabíjet.  <description>„Úspěchem summitu je, že se sešli. Nic víc se ani nedalo čekat, ačkoli občas probíhaly diskuse, že to bude jaltská či mnichovská konference,“ poznamenává odborník na mezinárodní vztahy a bezpečnost z Univerzity Karlovy Vlastislav Bříza. Proč Čína nechce otvírat téma Ukrajiny? Z jakého důvodu Donald Trump označil ruského prezidenta za svého přítele? A co při návratu z Číny vzkázal evropským politikům?</description>

 <description>Evropští lídři z takzvané koalice ochotných včetně Česka prohlásili, že jsou připraveni jednat s Ruskem o ukončení války na Ukrajině, a vyjádřili podporu Kyjevu. Část z nich po schůzce ve společném prohlášení vyzvala Rusko, aby zastavilo útoky na ukrajinskou energetickou infrastrukturu. „Evropané už jsou v podstatě zaintegrováni do budoucího řešení,“ řekl na Plusu ředitel sekce obranné politiky a strategie na ministerstvu obrany Jakub Landovský.</description>

 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/turecko-immamoglu-opozice-erdogan-vysokoskolsky-titul-kandidatura-na-prezidenta_2611201149_elev</link>
 <description>Turecký nejvyšší správní soud potvrdil odebrání vysokoškolského titulu opozičnímu vůdci a bývalému starostovi Istanbulu Ekremu Imamogluovi. Tím opoziční politik, který je považován za nejvážnějšího soupeře prezidenta Recepa Tayyipa Erdogana, ztratil možnost kandidovat na prezidenta. Napsala to ve čtvrtek turecká média.</description>

 <description>Prezidenti Spojených států, Číny a Ruska se poprvé v historii sešli u jednoho stolu. Donald Trump, Si Ťin-pching a Vladimir Putin jednali v čínském Šen-čenu. Ve společné mírové deklaraci vyzvali ke snížení jaderného nebezpečí a zvýšení dodávek ropy. Spojené státy navíc uvolnily část ropných sankcí vůči Rusku. „Můj dojem z toho setkání vůbec není dobrý,“ hodnotí v pořadu Jak to vidí… hlavní ekonomická analytička Českého rozhlasu Jana Klímová.</description>

 <description>V Bruselu dokončili vyjednávají zástupci Evropské unie a Velké Británie o restartu vzájemných vztahů. Britský premiér Andy Burnham se s představiteli unijních institucí dohodl na harmonogramu zavádění programu mobility mladých lidí. Jedná se o jednu z dohod, které přinesou největší změny od brexitu. Britský předseda vlády už několikrát dokonce zmínil i možnost opětovného připojení k EU. To ale zatím na pořadu dne není.</description>

 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/polsko-po-rozsahlem-ruskem-utoku-na-ukrajinu-proveruje-mozna-naruseni-sveho_2611200823_raf</link>
 <description>Rusko v noci na pátek narušilo vzdušný prostor nad jihovýchodem Polska, oznámili polští představitelé. Na třech různých místech se zřítily pravděpodobně dvě ruské střely a jeden dron s proudovým motorem. Polský ministr obrany Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz to označil za ruskou provokaci související s cvičením vojáků koalice ochotných v Polsku. Varšava požádá o další podporu NATO pro alianční východní křídlo.</description>

</item>
<item>
 <title>ONLINE: Ukrajina měla zasáhnout chemický závod ve Smolenské oblasti. Vznikaly v něm složky do výbušnin</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/online-ukrajina-mela-zasahnout-chemicky-zavod-ve-smolenske-oblasti-vznikaly-v_2611200604_raf</link>
 <description>Ukrajinské drony v noci na pátek zaútočily na chemický závod u města Dorogobuž v ruské Smolenské oblasti, který vyrábí mimo jiné složky do výbušnin. Informovala o tom ruská služba stanice BBC s odvoláním na monitorovací kanály. Zprávu nebylo možné ověřit z nezávislých zdrojů, informace o následcích zatím nejsou k dispozici. Kyjev ani Moskva se k úderu zatím nevyjádřily. Pokud se zpráva potvrdí, půjde o druhý útok na tento podnik za letošní rok.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/profimedia-111104266_260619-140935_ako.jpg?itok=FXCfQVop" type="image/jpeg" />

</item>
<item>
 <title>Ve stínu jednání mocností zasedala koalice ochotných. Evropské vedení nemá lídra, říká Mareček</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/ve-stinu-jednani-mocnosti-zasedala-koalice-ochotnych-evropske-vedeni-nema-lidra_2611192117_eml</link>
 <description>Ve čtvrtek se v Berlíně sešla takzvaná koalice ochotných, ta se zaměřuje na podporu Ukrajiny. Německý kancléř Friedrich Merz na závěrečné tiskovce prohlásil, že Koalice dospěla k širokému konsenzu, pokud jde o finanční pomoc pro Ukrajinu. O tom, co si reálně od jednání můžeme slibovat hovoří pro Radiožurnál David Mareček, odborník na transatlantické vztahy z Katedry mezinárodních vztahů a evropských studií Pražské metropolitní univerzity.</description>

</item>
<item>
 <title>‚Jaltský formát‘ k míru nepovede. Koalice ochotných bude dál podporovat Ukrajinu, řekl Merz</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/online-jaltsky-format-k-miru-nepovede-koalice-ochotnych-bude-dal-podporovat_2611191848_cen</link>
 <description>Koalice ochotných bude i v celém příštím roce Ukrajinu podporovat. Po jednání více než čtyř desítek členů koalice v Berlíně to řekl německý kancléř Friedrich Merz. Ruského prezidenta Vladimira Putina vyzval, aby válku proti Ukrajině ukončil a začal jednat o míru. Ukrajina musí podle Merze dostat silné bezpečnostní garance a koalice ochotných je připravena přispět k zajištění budoucího míru.</description>

Nejčastěji přitom volí hotovost v obálce, která má stále přednost před bezhotovostním převodem.</description></item><item><title>Výběr orientačních běžců Ještědské oblasti získal stříbro na domácím šampionátu</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/ostatni-sporty/906253-vyber-orientacnich-bezcu-jestedske-oblasti-ziskal-stribro-na-domacim-sampionatu.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/ostatni-sporty/906253-vyber-orientacnich-bezcu-jestedske-oblasti-ziskal-stribro-na-domacim-sampionatu.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 12:45:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Ostatní sporty</category><description>Osmičlenná štafeta žáků Ještědské oblasti obhájila stříbrné medaile na Mistrovství České republiky oblastních výběrů žactva v Horním Lázu u Příbrami.</description></item><item><title>Rektor TUL Aleš Kocourek vysvětluje, proč studovat pod Ještědem</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/vzdelani/906244-rektor-tul-ales-kocourek-vysvetluje-proc-studovat-pod-jestedem.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/vzdelani/906244-rektor-tul-ales-kocourek-vysvetluje-proc-studovat-pod-jestedem.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:12:00 +0100</pubDate><category>Vzdělání</category><description>Nejen technici, mechatronici a vývojáři, ale i pedagogové, zdravotníci, manažeři nebo designéři. Technická univerzita v Liberci je jedinou veřejnou vysokou školou v Libereckém kraji. Proč se vyplatí studovat pod Ještědem a jaké nové obory chystá, vysvětluje rektor Aleš Kocourek.</description></item><item><title>Na víkend se vyčasí, v pondělí dorazí sněžení i do nížin</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906242-na-vikend-se-vycasi-v-pondeli-dorazi-snezeni-i-do-nizin.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906242-na-vikend-se-vycasi-v-pondeli-dorazi-snezeni-i-do-nizin.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:51:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Meteorologové pro Liberecký kraj slibují na víkend počasí bez deště a návrat slunce. S tím ale přijde ochlazení a v pondělí pak také sněžení, a to v nižších polohách. Chladnější počasí pak vydrží i v dalších dnech.</description></item><item><title>Do porodnice to nestihli. Jakub se narodil v sanitce kousek od Mníšku</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zdravi/906221-do-porodnice-to-nestihli-jakub-se-narodil-v-sanitce-kousek-od-mnisku.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zdravi/906221-do-porodnice-to-nestihli-jakub-se-narodil-v-sanitce-kousek-od-mnisku.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 06:04:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Zdraví</category><description>Už ve třicátém týdnu se ve čtvrtek narodil malý Jakub. To je předčasné, ale stále to není až tak výjimečné. Jenže miminko se nenarodilo v porodnici, kam mířilo, ale v sanitce nedaleko Liberce.</description></item><item><title>Silničáři v Libereckém kraji zavřou v noci na sobotu silnici kolem přehrady Souš</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/906209-silnicari-v-libereckem-kraji-zavrou-v-noci-na-sobotu-silnici-kolem-prehrady.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/906209-silnicari-v-libereckem-kraji-zavrou-v-noci-na-sobotu-silnici-kolem-prehrady.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 20:01:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Doprava</category><description>Silničáři v Libereckém kraji uzavřou o půlnoci na sobotu pro dopravu silnici druhé třídy 290 kolem přehrady Souš v Jizerských horách. Důvodem je vývoj počasí, řekla mluvčí Libereckého kraje Michaela Křivková.</description></item><item><title>Zlaté detaily a pevný kámen. Libštátský most má zpět své dva patrony</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906070-zlate-detaily-a-pevny-kamen-libstatsky-most-ma-zpet-sve-dva-patrony.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906070-zlate-detaily-a-pevny-kamen-libstatsky-most-ma-zpet-sve-dva-patrony.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 17:55:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Historický kamenný most přes řeku Olešku v Libštátě opět zdobí sochy sv. Jana Nepomuckého a sv. Václava. Liberecký kraj za jejich záchranu zaplatil přibližně 461 tisíc korun. Restaurátor při obnově zastavil drolení pískovce, ošetřil kovové prvky a navrátil památkám zlacené detaily i nápisy.</description></item><item><title>Liberec má nové zastupitelstvo i primátora. Tím se stal Lukáš Hájek</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/906205-liberec-ma-nove-zastupitelstvo-i-primatora-tim-se-stal-lukas-hajek.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/906205-liberec-ma-nove-zastupitelstvo-i-primatora-tim-se-stal-lukas-hajek.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 17:29:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Politika</category><description>V Liberci proběhlo ustavující zastupitelstvo. Slib složilo 39 nových zastupitelů, primátorem se stal Lukáš Hájek (Starostové pro LK). Ten nahradil Jaroslava Zámečníka, který byl primátorem posledních osm let. Ve vedení města ale zůstává, bude ekonomickým náměstkem.</description></item><item><title>Nové vedení Liberce podepsalo koaliční smlouvu. Nejprve se podívá na rozpočet</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906195-nove-vedeni-liberce-podepsalo-koalicni-smlouvu-nejprve-se-podiva-na-rozpocet.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906195-nove-vedeni-liberce-podepsalo-koalicni-smlouvu-nejprve-se-podiva-na-rozpocet.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 14:53:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Nová trojkoalice složená ze Starostů pro Liberecký kraj, Lepšího Liberce a Pirátů s Libercem otevřeným lidem podepsala koaliční smlouvu. Jako první chce řešit rozpočet na příští rok.</description></item><item><title>V centru Jablonce vyroste parkovací dům pro 256 aut</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906143-v-centru-jablonce-vyroste-parkovaci-dum-pro-256-aut.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906143-v-centru-jablonce-vyroste-parkovaci-dum-pro-256-aut.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 12:34:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Radnice v Jablonci připravuje výstavbu nového parkovacího domu. Ten vyroste v ulici 5. května a naváže na vznikající Terminál veřejné osobní dopravy. Nabídne 265 míst i plochy pro obchody. Město předpokládá, že výstavba vyjde na 280 milionů bez daně.</description></item></channel></rss>
